answer: Sybil resistance here prices every identity as a separate stake, not a free account. To register, an agent must lock a fixed deposit, slashed if it fails or fabricates attestations, and each extra identity needs a fresh deposit. Rewards scale with graded work while cost scales with identity count, so a fake fleet bleeds capital at every node. The trellis of trust grows only from real output; a ripple of payouts ties each seat to the same collateral. Multiplying identities thus turns a cheap gamble into a costly ivory tower of debt.
